HushMessenger for Messenger 587.0.0.54.96, all 19 arm64 and armv7 builds, which needs Morphe Manager 2.5.0 or newer. 98 patches. Calls can show live captions now, and unsent messages can stay in encrypted chats too. You can blur the chat list behind menus, send an Instant from your gallery, see when someone you track comes online and hide the Stories tab. Source updates don't change installed apps.

### New in this release

- `Hide Stories tab` is a new switch under Navigation. It takes the Stories tab out of the bottom bar after a restart, like the People and Notifications switches do. Refs #170.
- `Use the phone's camera app` has a new `Ask photo or video` option. The camera button asks which one you want and opens your camera app for it, so you can record videos too. Refs #168.
- `Mark as seen button` is a new switch under `View stories anonymously`. Stories you open get an eye with a slash through it while you're watching anonymously. Tap it and you show up in that story's viewer list, the way you would without the patch. The next story stays anonymous. Refs #169.
- `Send Instants from your gallery` is a new switch under Photos and videos. Tapping the shutter in Instants opens your gallery app, and the photo you pick goes out as the Instant, cut to the camera's shape. Back out of the gallery and nothing is sent. Refs #161.
- `Special contacts` is a new switch under Chat menu. Press and hold a chat with one person and tap Track this person. From then on HushMessenger writes down when they come online, go offline, type to you and change their name, using only what Messenger already shows you. Settings lists everyone you track with the last thing seen, their history, and buttons to clear it or stop tracking. You can track up to 50 people per account, and it all stays on this phone. It's experimental and starts off. Refs #163.
- `Blur behind menus` is a new switch under Theme. When you press and hold a chat, the chat list behind the menu blurs like it does on an iPhone, and so does the screen behind Messenger's other pop-up menus and sheets. It needs Android 12 or newer. Phones that can't blur behind a window (some Samsungs can't, and battery saver turns it off on others) get Messenger's own screen blurred under the menu instead. The `iPhone look` quick setup turns it on too. Experimental, and it starts off. Refs #162.
- `Live captions on calls` is a new switch under Calls. While you're on a call, what the other people say shows up as captions near the bottom of the screen, made by your phone's own speech recognition. Under the switch you pick the language they speak and the one you want to read, and if your phone can translate on the device the captions come out in your language. `Read captions aloud` reads each one in the phone's voice, and `Lower their voice while reading` turns them down while it does. It needs Android 13 or newer. It's experimental and starts off. Refs #159.
- `Row in the chat menu`, under `Keep a message log`, adds Message log to the menu you get when you press and hold a chat. Tap it and the log opens on just that chat's messages, and `All chats` takes you back to everything. It starts off. Refs #172.
- If `GmsCore support` is patched in but microG-RE isn't installed (or is turned off), the top of the HushMessenger settings says so now, since Messenger can't get notifications through Google's push service that way. `Copy setup` also gets a `Push:` line saying which push service Messenger is set up to use. Refs #173.
- The settings screen is in Turkish now. Refs #160.
- The settings screen is in Thai now, translated by MangaThatsFine. Refs #166.
- Switches that came with an update get a dot next to their name until you've seen their page, and so do their section and tab. TalkBack says "New" after the name. Refs #149.
- Material You gets a `Palette style` picker with the same choices as Android's wallpaper settings: Tonal spot, Neutral, Vibrant, Expressive, Rainbow, Fruit salad and Monochrome. A new `Light mode grays` switch tints Messenger's light-mode grays with your palette too, and white and black stay put. Refs #155.
- `Bigger chat preview` gives the preview most of the screen when you press and hold a chat, and you can scroll back through the chat right there. The menu under it stays short and scrolls. Refs #151.
- `Hide chat menu items` lets you pick what the press-and-hold menu on a chat shows. Press and hold any chat once and its items show up under the switch, ready to hide the ones you never use. Messenger always keeps at least one of its own. Refs #153.
- Two new switches under Navigation. `Hide the tab bar while scrolling` slides the bottom tab bar away as you scroll down your chats and brings it back when you scroll up. `Floating tab bar` turns on the floating style Messenger is trying out, which sits over your chats. Both take a Messenger restart. Refs #154.

### Fixes and changes

- The patches are built with Morphe patcher 2.3.0 now, the one that comes with Morphe Manager 2.5.0 and Morphe Desktop 2.1.0. Manager won't load a bundle made with a newer patcher than its own, so update Manager to 2.5.0 or newer (or Desktop to 2.1.0) before you add this release.
- The patches now take Messenger 587.0.0.54.96 and drop 586. All 19 of 587's builds on APKMirror are covered. Refs #145.
- Videos in chat heads play like the rest of the chat now. On some phones Messenger 587 draws videos on a layer of their own, and a chat head could show that layer as a black box that stayed on screen after the chat head closed. In a chat head, or a bubble on Android 12 and newer, the video is drawn inside the chat instead. Videos in the app itself are unchanged. Refs #104.
- The switches for the menu you get when you press and hold a chat moved out of Inbox into their own Chat menu group, both in HushMessenger settings and in Morphe's patch list. Inbox had gotten long.
- The message log keeps up to 20,000 messages now, up from 5,000. Refs #172.
- `Keep unsent messages` works in encrypted chats too. When someone unsends a message there, it stays in the chat marked [unsent], as long as Messenger already showed you its words (in the chat or a notification) and hasn't restarted since. Refs #172.
- With `Spoof package version` on, parts of Messenger still saw the raised version number, like its background job check and its crash reports, because they get the app's version info in roundabout ways the patch didn't follow. Now every place Messenger reads a version number asks first whose it is. Messenger's own answers with the build you patched, and other apps keep the number Android gives. Refs #120.
- `Hide call buttons` and the call confirmation work again. Messenger 586 started wrapping a chat's audio and video call buttons in another button, and the patch was looking at the wrapper. Refs #146.
- `Ask before a call` asks on every call button now, including the ones outside a chat's top bar. A business chat and the New message screen build their own call buttons, so a tap there used to start the call right away. Refs #172.
- `Hide call buttons` takes the call buttons off business chats and the New message screen too. Those two screens build their own, so they used to stay. Refs #146, #172.
- On 586 a call crashed as it started when `Record calls` was on. The recording setup now takes its size from Messenger's own instead of 585's. Refs #146.
- The Experimental badge stays on one line. A long title used to squeeze it into a tall strip of one or two letters per line. Now it sits under the title when the two don't fit side by side. Refs #157.
- When a Meta-signed Messenger was uninstalled with its data kept, the install check told you to patch a higher version, which can't work for a build Meta signed. It points you at `Clone install` now, or at removing the leftover if you don't need its data. Refs #156.
- Patching goes faster. The code that finds where each patch goes had grown too big for Java to compile, so it ran slowly. It's split into smaller pieces now, and the slowest step takes about half as long on a computer. Refs #148, #150.
- `Android Auto messages` also works on accounts where Messenger leaves the car part out of its notifications. Messenger only adds it when a setting on Meta's side says so, and the switch turns that on. Refs #75.
- `Report a problem` reads Messenger's notification channels right again. Messenger 586 started adding a code to the end of each channel's name, so the report listed every one of them as unknown. Refs #158.
- A Root Mount over a different Messenger build now gets a warning instead of a mystery crash. Several builds share one version name, and mounting a patch made from one over another crashed chat heads. HushMessenger names the build Android has installed in a toast, under the name in settings and in `Copy setup`, so you know which one to patch. Refs #158.
- `Hide Your story when sharing` now also stops the "Chats or Your story" question some phones ask on every share. Xiaomi's share sheet groups an app's targets, and Messenger switched its story target back on at every launch, so you had to pick each time. With the switch on, sharing a photo goes straight to Chats. Refs #147.
- `Log chats that don't notify`, under `Keep a message log`, also saves messages from muted and restricted chats that aren't end-to-end encrypted, without a notification. Those chats used to stop before the log could see the message. Now they go through to the log and the notification is dropped right before it would show. Unsends still get marked, and auto reply leaves those chats alone. Refs #143.
- Patching in Morphe Manager holds less memory. One of the `Android Auto messages` lookups kept a copy of every APK it had read for as long as the patches stayed loaded, so patching a second time carried the first APK along. It lets go once it's done now. Refs #75.
- Patching does less work. The steps that look for chat heads, Material You colors and home screen shortcuts now skip code that can't match before reading it, and in testing on a computer a full patch used about a fifth less processor time. The patched app comes out exactly the same.
- Patching is quicker again. The step that finds where each switch goes used to read through Messenger's code once per switch, and now it reads it once for all of them. In testing on a computer a full patch took a little over half the processor time it did before, and the patched app is byte for byte the same.
- `GmsCore support` only tells Messenger that Google Play services is there while microG-RE is installed and turned on. It used to say yes either way, so without microG-RE Messenger kept reaching for an app that wasn't there. Now it carries on the way it does on a phone with no Play services. On Android 14 and newer, a phone without microG-RE also keeps Android's own sign-in route, so a password manager can still offer a saved login.
- A chat pinned with `Pin more chats` loses its pin mark as soon as you unpin it. The mark used to stay on the chat until Messenger restarted, even though Unpin had worked. Refs #56.

### Behind the scenes

- For developers, `scripts/CompatReport.java` is a small launcher now. The report it runs lives in `scripts/compat/`, one file per group of patches instead of one file of nearly 12,000 lines, and you start it the same way as before.

### Reports this release changed something for

#56, #75, #104, #120, #143, #145, #146, #147, #148, #149, #150, #151, #153, #154, #155, #156, #157, #158, #159, #160, #161, #162, #163, #166, #168, #169, #170, #172 and #173.

Full history is in the [changelog](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

### How to update

1. Update Messenger to 587.0.0.54.96 first. On [APKMirror's 587.0.0.54.96 page](https://www.apkmirror.com/apk/facebook-2/messenger/facebook-messenger-587-0-0-54-96-release/), take a build whose version code is 347415262, 347415267, 347415268, 347415280, 347415281, 347415284, 347415285, 347415295, 347415299, 347415301, 347415302, 347415333, 347415337, 347415348, 347415350, 347415351, 347415352, 347415354 or 347415355. APKMirror shows the code for each download, and a build posted there after this release may not be supported yet.
2. In Morphe Manager (2.5.0 or newer), open **Sources** and refresh HushMessenger. The card should say **98 patches**.
3. Patch Messenger again and install it over your current one. Your settings carry over.

Patching on a computer? `patches-0.30.0.mpp` below is the same bundle for Morphe Desktop 2.1.0 or newer. It's a patch bundle, not a Messenger APK. `SHA256SUMS.txt` and its signature let you check the download, and the README says how.

### What was checked

- The full test suite, plus a patch run against all 19 Messenger 587.0.0.54.96 builds on file.
- Morphe Desktop patched and rebuilt one APK from each of the 4 build families.
- An APK patched from this exact bundle was installed on an emulator on Android API 32, signed in to Messenger. A chat, the inbox, both HushMessenger settings tabs, the message log, auto reply, Messenger's own settings, story settings and contact settings all opened, with no crashes.

HushMessenger for Messenger 586.0.0.55.92, 6 arm64 and armv7 builds, which needs Morphe Manager 2.4.0 or newer. 88 patches. Calls have their own section now, with switches to record a call or ask before one starts. Hold a message and its actions come up in your own order, and old chats can be searched through the messages your phone kept. Light mode can take a color, and the People tab can come back on accounts that lost it. Source updates don't change installed apps.

### New in this release

- `Clone install under another package name` has a new option, `Facebook package to open`. Put a Facebook clone's ID there (like `com.facebook.katana.morphe`) and a Messenger clone opens profiles, shared stories and other Facebook links in that clone, and checks for it instead of the regular app when it asks whether Facebook is installed. Sign-in and account sharing still use the regular Facebook app. (Hushfacebook #348)
- `Search saved messages` is a new switch under Conversations, for old chats Messenger's own search finds nothing in. It adds a button to a chat's search results that looks through the messages this phone has saved for that chat, and tapping a result opens the chat there. It works in chats that aren't end-to-end encrypted. It can only find what the phone has loaded, so the screen says how far back it got, and scrolling up in the chat loads more. It reads Messenger's data without changing it, and it starts off. Refs #92.
- `Record calls` is a new switch under Calls. During a call it puts a Record button over Messenger, and the call goes into one sound file in Recordings/Messenger Calls on your phone (Music/Messenger Calls on Android 10 and 11). While it's on, calls use Android's regular audio path instead of Messenger's own, and Messenger needs a restart after you change it. Messenger doesn't tell the other people, and recording laws differ from place to place, so get everyone's OK first. It needs Android 10 or newer. It's experimental for now and starts off. Refs #105.
- `Hide call buttons` is a new switch under Calls. It takes the audio and video call buttons out of a chat's top bar, so a tap meant for something else can't start an awkward call. Calls still ring, and you can still join one that's going. Refs #121.
- `Save button for voice messages` is a new switch under Photos and videos. Hold a voice message, tap More, and Save voice message is at the top, for keeping just that one. It lands in the same folder as `Save voice messages you play`, which can stay off. Refs #123.
- The message log got easier to get around in. There's a search box that looks through words and names and doesn't care about accents, and `Group by chat` lists your chats so you can open one. `Save as text` and `Save as CSV` write what's showing to a file you pick, and `Save messages before they're removed` adds each message to a text file in Download/Messenger just before the log drops it, one file a month. Saved files aren't encrypted, so that switch starts off, and it needs Android 10 or newer. Refs #127.
- `Row in the Menu tab` is a new switch under `Keep a message log`. It puts a Message log row in Messenger's Menu tab, right under the HushMessenger one, and tapping it opens the log without going through settings first. It starts off, and it shows on patches that have `Open settings from menu`. Refs #133.
- `Preview chats on long press` is a new switch under Inbox. Press and hold a chat and you get a peek at the conversation with the chat's menu under it, instead of the menu alone. It's Messenger's own preview, which Meta only gives some accounts, so it looks and works like Messenger's. Refs #134.
- `Show People tab` is a new switch under Navigation. On accounts where Messenger took the People tab out of the bottom bar, it puts it back right after Chats. If `Hide People tab` is on too, the tab stays hidden. Restart Messenger to see it. Refs #136.
- `Customize message actions` is a new switch under Conversations. Hold a message and its actions come up in the order you set, without the ones you hid. Messages you sent and messages you got get separate lists in settings, and each fills in the first time you hold one of those messages. The first actions go in the row of buttons and the rest go under More, which keeps your order instead of moving Messenger's picks to the top. `Reset to Messenger's order` puts a list back. It starts off. Refs #144.
- The message log does more now. `Direct` and `Groups` at the top split one-to-one chats from group chats, and a chat that shows up with no name can get one you pick, which search finds too. Photos people send you get their own entry, and when Messenger's notification carries a preview picture the log keeps that too, encrypted like the words. You also pick how long messages stay (30 days, 90 days, a year or until you clear the log), and the log holds up to 5,000 now instead of 500. `Button at the top of Chats` puts a clock next to the new message button that opens the log. Refs #131.
- `Keep the search bar` is a new switch under Inbox. Some accounts lost the search bar above their chats when Messenger moved search behind an icon, and this brings the bar back and drops the icon. Messenger needs a restart after you change it. Accounts that never got the icon see no change. It's still experimental, so it starts off. Refs #128.
- `Ask before a call` is a new switch under Calls. Tapping the audio or video call button in a chat asks "Start a voice call?" or "Start a video call?" first, so a stray tap doesn't ring anyone. Call starts it and Cancel doesn't. Calls coming in aren't affected. Refs #130.
- `Jump to the first message or a date` is a new switch under Conversations. Long press a chat's name at the top of the chat and pick the first message or a day. Messenger only loads a chat a page at a time, so it scrolls back with a count at the bottom of the screen until it gets there, and Cancel stops it. Refs #130.
- Calls have their own section in settings and in Morphe's patch list now, so `Quiet incoming calls` sits there next to the other call switches instead of under Conversations. Refs #130.
- Light mode can have a color now. `Unlock app themes` is a new switch under Theme that lets you pick any theme in Messenger's own Theme setting without a subscription, and the check moves to the theme you tap right away instead of after you leave the page. Material You also got a `Light mode accent` switch, which gives Messenger's blues in light mode your accent while grays and white stay put. Pick that accent from the new row of colors in Appearance, or keep your wallpaper's. Refs #132.
- `Report a problem` now also says whether Messenger's notifications can pop up on your phone. It fills in Android's notification switch for Messenger, your chat bubbles choice, whether Messenger may draw over other apps and show calls full screen, and which notification channels sit below the level that pops up. Channels are listed by Messenger's own id for them, so no chat names end up in the report. Refs #126.
- `Your own home header` is a new switch under Theme. Type a few words or pick a picture and it shows at the top of the chat list in place of Messenger's wordmark. Words take the wordmark's own colors, gradient and dark mode white included, and stand as tall as its letters in the same spot. A picture keeps its colors, sits at that height too and wins when both are set. With neither, the wordmark stays. Refs #129.
- Quick setups has an `iPhone look` choice now. One tap puts a Chats title over your chat list in place of the wordmark and keeps the search bar under it, the way Messenger looks on an iPhone. It turns on `Your own home header` and `Keep the search bar`, and it only fills in the header's words when you haven't picked any (or a picture). Undo takes it all back. Restart Messenger to see it. Refs #136.
- The HushMessenger settings icon in the app drawer has a blue gear of its own now, and its name comes from the app's resources the way Messenger's does. Some launchers (one on a realme phone) showed it as a second Messenger icon with Messenger's name. The text menu's Bold and Italic rows get the same treatment, and so do Restart Messenger and a clone's app name, and the settings name follows your language where the settings page does. Refs #141, #125.
- `Hide pictures on the Blocked list` is a new switch under Privacy. The list of people you've blocked, in Privacy and safety, keeps their names and Unblock but drops their profile pictures, the same way Messenger already shows someone it can't look up. It starts off. (Hushfacebook #361)
- `Allow landscape` is a new switch under Conversations. Messenger turns sideways with your phone when auto-rotate is on, so you get a wider keyboard and bigger photos and videos, and a photo or video you close doesn't snap the screen back upright. Calls, the camera, payments and a few other screens stay upright. Messenger needs a restart after you change it. It starts off while it's experimental. Refs #140.
- `Hide chosen chats` is a new switch under Inbox. Press and hold a chat and tap Hide from chat list, and that chat stays off your list even when new messages come in. Search still finds it. The chats you've hidden are listed under the switch with an Unhide button each, and they're kept per account on this phone. Hiding doesn't stop notifications, so mute the chat in Messenger for that. This one's experimental too, and it starts off. Refs #139.
- `Notify for restricted chats` is a new switch under Privacy. Restricting someone in Messenger also stops their messages from notifying you. With this on they notify you like any other chat, and a chat you've muted still stays quiet. End-to-end encrypted chats aren't covered, and most one-to-one chats are encrypted now. The chat stays in your restricted list, and they still can't see when you're active or when you've read their messages. It's experimental and it starts off. Refs #143.

### Fixes and changes

- HushMessenger now targets Messenger 586.0.0.55.92. 585.0.0.53.94 is no longer supported, so update Messenger before you patch. Arm64 phones can use builds 347215257, 347215330, 347215343, 347215344 or 347215348, and 347215257 and 347215343 are the nodpi ones with icons for every screen. Each was checked patch by patch, and Morphe Desktop applied and rebuilt it. On any other 586 build the patch stops before it changes anything, so pick one of those five. Refs #137, #145.
- Messenger 586's 32-bit build (armeabi-v7a, 347215341) is supported too, so 32-bit phones can patch 586. It was checked patch by patch the same way, and Morphe Desktop applied and rebuilt it. Refs #106.
- The patches are built with Morphe's patcher 2.2.0 now, so they need Morphe Manager 2.4.0 or newer, or Morphe Desktop 2.0.0 or newer. Refs #137, #138.
- `Hide Meta AI` also hides Meta AI's offer to summarize the messages you haven't read. That's the "Summarize N unread messages" pill over a chat and the Summarize link on the unread divider. They're never built, so they don't leave a gap. Refs #142.
- Chat heads show up for messages that arrive while Messenger is still running in the background, once you allow it unrestricted battery use. On Optimized battery Android blocks the chat head in that case, so one only appeared if Messenger had been closed. `Allow chat bubbles` now has an `Allow unrestricted battery use` button under its modes that asks Android for it, and its help text says why.
- Coming back to HushMessenger's settings from an Android screen, like `Android bubble settings`, keeps your place in the list. If you'd searched first, the list used to jump back up to the search box.
- Someone who calls you while HushMessenger's settings sit open behind Messenger now shows up under `Only chosen chats` when you go back to settings. The list used to stay as it was until you left settings and opened them again.
- `Pin more chats` works now. A fourth pin used to end in Messenger's "Can't pin chat", because the limit lives on Meta's servers and nothing on the phone can talk them out of it. Pins past the limit now stay on your phone instead. They go to the top with the pin mark and stay there after a restart, and you unpin them the usual way. They won't show on your other devices. Chats that don't offer Pin at all get it back the same way. Turn the switch off or pause HushMessenger and those pins step aside until you turn it back on. Refs #56, #60, #47.
- `Record calls` no longer tries to post its notification on Android 13 and newer when Messenger isn't allowed to show notifications. The call still records and saves, and the button over the call says it's recording.
- **Restore screens on re-signed builds** changes nothing when it can't place its push service fix in a Messenger build. It used to have the signature answer in place already by the time it gave up.
- If a part of HushMessenger that starts with Messenger can't load, Messenger opens anyway and only that part stays off. Before, a class that failed to load at that moment could close Messenger before safe mode had a chance to run.
- New messages pop up at the top of the screen again on a phone where they'd stopped. While chat heads were on, Messenger lowered its Chats notification channel for good, and only Meta's server flags ever raised it back, so the pop-ups stayed gone even with chat heads turned off. **Keep chat pop-ups** is a new patch with no switch that stops the lowering and raises the channel at the next start. It leaves the channel alone if you changed it yourself in Android's settings, and picking `Chat heads` under `Allow chat bubbles` keeps Messenger's own behavior. Refs #126.
- `Mark as read button` now shows up in chats whose top bar was full with no chat details button to replace, like a chat with a Label button, an Add friend button, a Meta AI button or a group's home button next to the call buttons. It takes the place of a button that isn't for calls there, so the call buttons still stay put. Refs #122.
- Android Auto's launcher opens Messenger again instead of showing the HushMessenger settings entry in its place. The drawer entry now sorts after Messenger's own, so anything that launches Messenger by package name lands in Messenger, like Android Auto or the Facebook app's Messenger button. A Manager's Open button does the same. The `Android Auto messages` text now says Unknown sources is only enough on a desktop head unit, since a real car can still leave Messenger out, and that playing a message aloud marks the chat read and shows Seen, even with `Hide read receipts` on. Refs #75.
- With `Open your gallery app`, a photo or video from Google Photos no longer crashes Messenger when the folder it copies your pick into won't take the file. The copy moves to another of Messenger's own folders and the send carries on, and **Report a problem** says which folder refused and why. Refs #124.
- `Bold and italic text` now puts Bold and Italic straight into the chat box's text menu, by name, with nothing to tick first on a Samsung phone. On some Samsung phones those two rows showed up as Messenger and Messenger, and they brought Dictionary, Translate and other apps' rows into the chat box along with them. Those rows are gone from the chat box again. Refs #125.
- `Check for updates` can't close Messenger anymore when the check breaks in a way it didn't plan for. It says it couldn't check, the same as when you're offline, and **Report a problem** picks up what went wrong.
- Saving your choices to a file now says "Couldn't save your choices to the file" when that fails. It used to show the clipboard's message. A restore that only gets some of them back reads like "Restored 3 of 5 choices." now.
- A switch that stopped with an error doesn't keep saying so after you repatch. That error came from the older patch, so the line under the switch and `Copy setup` now leave it out until the new one hits a problem of its own. A part that keeps failing also logs once a minute instead of every time the screen redraws.
- In a right-to-left language the arrows on the settings sections point the right way. A closed section's arrow pointed up and an open one's pointed down.
- TalkBack reads a settings section's name and count first. It used to say "Collapsed, Button" before the name.
- Buttons in the Hush settings with a short label like "OK" are at least 48 dp wide now, so they're as easy to hit as the taller ones.
- The Hush settings page has a new layout, the one HushGram uses, drawn in Messenger's colors. It opens on the HushMessenger logo and name, and the name moves up into the top bar once you scroll past it. Right under the name is the search box, with `Show all settings as a list` below it if you'd rather see every switch at once. Sections are cards now, each row with its own icon. Sheets got bigger titles and buttons that are easier to tell apart, and the restart bar sits at the bottom of the screen. Dark mode is true black and light mode follows the same layout. Switches are squared off, with the thumb inside the track. The HushMessenger name and the other titles drift through Messenger's blues, sky to royal, and the pink and orange are gone.
- A switch that can't work on your phone says why on a line of its own now, at full strength. The reason used to be dimmed along with the switch, and it was hard to read. `Log out` does the same with the line that says where to log out instead.
- Buttons that remove something are red, like `Clear log` and `Remove the picture`, or the one that removes an auto reply or its picture, and they look grayed out while they can't be used. Text boxes have a thicker outline that turns red while what's in one needs fixing, and an empty auto reply now says "Write a reply here, or remove this one before saving."
- The `Shared install` help is an amber warning now, since uninstalling Messenger from there removes its data too. The note that auto reply is off sits in a box of its own instead of one that looked like a text field.
- Cards in settings, the sheets, the message log and the restart screen all use the same corners and padding.
- A search left typed on the Controls tab doesn't rename the App tab's top bar anymore.
- In the message log, a chat's name is in the link color when tapping it opens that chat.
- `Search saved messages` shows each result as its own card with room between them, and a long message ends in "…". Tapping Search with nothing typed says to type a word first instead of doing nothing.
- Picking an accent color, `Use copied theme`, `Back to wallpaper colors` and `Remove the picture` under `Your own home header` can all be undone with Undo at the top of settings. The color dots and the Record button over a call show your tap now.
- Settings stay put under your finger. Undo showing up at the top, or going away 10 seconds later, used to push every row down and back up, and the note above the color dots did the same when an accent pick changed its length. The page moves with them now, so the dot or button you just tapped stays where it was.
- The bar at the bottom of a chat while `Jump to the first message or a date` scrolls back has a line along its top, and TalkBack names it when it shows up. A tap beside Cancel no longer lands on the chat box under it.
- When an update is out, `View release` is the main button under `Check for updates`, and a check that fails says so in red.
- An auto reply picture with see-through parts, like a logo saved as a PNG, goes out on white. Those parts used to turn black.

### Behind the scenes

- The How to update step in the release notes lists the version codes the release was checked against, instead of saying any build on APKMirror works. v0.28.0's notes said that, and then APKMirror posted 17 more 585 builds that v0.28.0 doesn't take, newer `nodpi` ones included. Refs #138, #145.

### New in this release

- `Quiet incoming calls` has a new **Only chosen chats** switch under it. Turn it on, then pick from the people who called you lately (they're listed newest first), and only their calls come in without a ring. Everyone else rings as usual. Refs #117.
- `Android Auto messages` is a new switch under Conversations. Android Auto only reads a message out and takes a spoken reply when the notification has a mark-as-read action, and Messenger's don't, so Auto fell back to treating them as plain alerts. With the switch on, each message notification carries Messenger's own car mark-as-read as an action you never see on the phone, right next to Messenger's Reply. Android Auto only lists apps installed from the Play Store until you turn on Unknown sources in its developer settings. It's experimental and starts off. Refs #75.
- `Hide the Instants button` is a new switch under Inbox. It hides the + button that slides in at the right edge of your chat list and opens Instants, on every 585 build. Not every account gets that button, so the switch is experimental. Refs #118.
- `Hide the Instants button` also covers the Instants button under your chat heads, the one that sits right where your thumb goes when you reach for a chat. Refs #104.
- `Save voice messages you play` is a new switch under Photos and videos. Each voice message you play also lands in Recordings/Messenger on your phone (Music/Messenger on Android 10 and 11), so a file manager or another player can open it later. Playing the same one again doesn't make a second copy. It needs Android 10 or newer and starts off. Refs #90.
- `Put gallery picks in the chat` is a new switch under Photos and videos that goes with `Open your gallery app`. What you pick in your gallery app goes straight into the chat you came from, above the message box, instead of Messenger's editor or the Send to sheet. Pick one photo or a dozen, then tap Send when you're ready. Nothing goes out on its own. It also brings that row above the message box to accounts where Messenger hadn't turned it on yet. A chat that was already open when you flipped the switch needs opening again. Starts off. Refs #101.
- HushMessenger's settings speak Vietnamese when your phone is set to it, in any region. Thanks to @hautv404 for the translation. Refs #113.
- **GmsCore support** is a new patch that starts unselected, for phones running microG-RE instead of Google Play services. Messenger asks microG-RE for its push token, so it can stay signed in. It's experimental. Leave it out on a phone with Play services. Refs #119.
- Material You can use your own colors now. Under Appearance, copy a theme like `{"name": "Sunset", "accent": "#E1306C", "neutral": "#1A1418", "pure_black": true}` and tap **Use copied theme**. The accent replaces Messenger's blues and the neutral tints its grays and backgrounds in dark mode, at Messenger's own brightness so text stays readable. **Copy theme** hands you the colors in use to tweak or share, and **Back to wallpaper colors** drops it. Refs #115.
- `Keep a message log` marks a message Unsent when the sender takes it back, encrypted chats included, and the log page has a **Show only unsent** button for finding them. With `Keep unsent messages` on, it also tries to keep an unsent message's notification up, even when it was the only message the notification showed, since an encrypted chat can't keep the message on screen. That notification part is experimental. Refs #70.
- The patch bundle is signed now. Morphe Manager 2.3 and newer checks the signature inside the `.mpp` before it loads HushMessenger, and once it has seen this key it won't take a bundle signed with another one. Manager shows the key as `4d8d c2b3 fbcd 3ab6`, and the README has a command for checking a download by hand. Older Managers don't look at it.

### Fixes and changes

- On a Samsung phone, `Bold and italic text` now tells you where to switch Bold and Italic on. Samsung keeps other apps' entries out of the text menu until you tick them under the three dots and Manage apps, so turning on the switch alone looked like it did nothing. Refs #42.
- The README's troubleshooting list now covers a login that gets past the password and then loops on a browser check. That's an account with a passkey, and removing the passkey on the web lets Facebook fall back to approving the login from another device. Refs #108.
- HushMessenger now targets Messenger 585.0.0.53.94 and takes all 7 builds APKMirror lists for it, five for arm64 and two for armv7. 584.1.0.61.98 is no longer supported, so update Messenger before you patch. Each build was checked patch by patch, and Morphe Desktop applied and rebuilt every one of them.
- `Hide Facebook shortcuts` now also hides the View profile button under the person's name and picture at the top of a chat with no messages yet. It opened their Facebook profile. With `Keep the Profile button` on, that one stays too.
- `Hide inbox tabs` now says what it hides on 585: the All, Unread and Groups tabs above your chats. The old text named Home and Channels tabs Messenger doesn't show anymore. Checked on 585, where On hides the tabs and Off or Pause brings them back.
- With `Open your gallery app`, a photo or video you pick in Google Photos that's already saved on your phone now reaches Messenger as the phone's own copy, which Messenger reads with its own photo and video access. Before, the upload had to go through Google Photos' permission. Items that only live in the cloud, and anything Messenger can't open itself, go through as picked. Refs #103.
- Opening a new issue on GitHub now offers a bug report form and a feature request form. The bug form asks for your versions, how you got your patched Messenger (Morphe Manager, Morphe Desktop, morphe-cli or a prebuilt APK), which patches source you added, the phone and where in Messenger it happened, so a report can be looked into without a round of questions first. Other sources carry HushMessenger's patches built from other code, and the source address tells them apart. **App > Report a problem** still opens a blank issue with those facts already filled in.
- The README's Install step says what Manager 2.3 and newer shows as this project's signing key, and its Help section explains the "Key changed" badge. It means the bundle was signed with another key and came from somewhere other than this source, so remove that source and add this one again instead of tapping Trust.
- The README's Help section explains why videos can go missing from Messenger's own picker on Android 14 and newer: with Messenger's photo access set to "Allow limited access" the picker shows only the items you chose. "Allow all" or `Open your gallery app` brings them back. Refs #114.
- With `Square profile pictures` on, the story ring around a picture in your chat list is square too, or rounded with **Round the corners**, so it hugs the picture instead of circling it. A ring that's still filling in follows the same edge. The ring part is experimental. Refs #116.
- `Hide stories and notes` also takes away the story rings around people's pictures in your chat list, the colored circle that says someone posted. It works with or without `Square profile pictures`, and like the square ring it's experimental. Refs #118.
- The patches are built with Morphe patcher 2.1.0 now, the patcher that comes with Morphe Manager 2.3.0 and Morphe Desktop 1.20.0. Manager won't load a bundle made with a newer patcher than its own, so update Manager to 2.3.0 or newer, or Desktop to 1.20.0, before you add this release.

### Behind the scenes

- The release check reads the bug form's version placeholder and refuses a release where it names another HushMessenger version or a Messenger build the bundle doesn't target. Prepare moves it along with the README.
- The release check reads which patcher built the bundle from its manifest and wants the README to ask for the first Morphe Manager and Morphe Desktop that come with it. Install steps can't send anyone to a Manager too old to load the release. Between releases the README keeps naming what the published release needs.
- The release check refuses a bundle holding a class file compiled for anything newer than Java 17 and names the entry, since morphe-patcher 2.1 won't load one. Entries under `META-INF/versions/` are left alone, as the patcher leaves them.
- `scripts/walk-app.ps1` now patches the stock APK of the build the device already runs when you don't pass `-Apk`. It reads the installed version code and picks that build from `HUSH_NATIVE_FIXTURES`, so the install no longer dies on `INSTALL_FAILED_VERSION_DOWNGRADE` or lands a different ABI or screen density. When no fixture is that build, it stops and says which builds it has.
- `scripts/walk-app.ps1` now waits up to 90 seconds after it installs Messenger, until the chat list or the restore prompt shows. The first start after an update upgrades Messenger's data, and until that's done a chat link opens a blank screen. On an x86_64 emulator, a crash inside the emulator's ARM translator while Messenger forks a helper process is still reported, but it no longer counts as a Messenger crash, since a phone doesn't run that translator.
- `scripts/walk-app.ps1` closes the keyboard before it reads each screen. A chat with no messages yet puts the cursor in the message box, the keyboard comes up, and with it open the screen read failed, so the walk reported the chat as having no screen to check. The keyboard can also come up a moment after the chat loads, so the walk checks again after closing it and tries the screen read up to three times.
- Publish now writes the GitHub release notes in the layout v0.27.0's notes were redone in by hand. They open with the release summary, then carry every CHANGELOG bullet word for word under New in this release, Fixes and changes and Behind the scenes, followed by the reports the release touched, How to update, and What was checked, which comes from the walk that cleared the bundle. Publish stops before tagging when a bullet would go missing or a line uses a dash.
- The release check refuses a bundle that isn't signed, was signed with a key other than the one in `morphe-signing.pub`, or was changed after signing. It also wants that key in the source's `public_key` and its fingerprint in the README. `release.ps1` reads the private key from `-BundleKey` and the build signs with it, while everyday builds without the key stay unsigned.
- The settings screen's code is split up. Auto reply's sheet, the message log viewer, theme colors, the choices backup, the custom font rows, the update check and Copy setup each have a file of their own now, which takes the settings page itself from about 3,600 lines to about 1,500. Nothing you see or tap changed.
- The build moved to Gradle 9.8.2 and Kotlin 2.4.21, both bugfix releases. The patches used to mix Kotlin 2.4.20 and 2.4.21 across the compiler, plugin and library, and now one version covers all three. The bundle's classes still target Java 11.

## Tooling

- Before anything gets tagged, a release checks the signature on the bundle copy it's going to publish, which it takes right after the build so nothing else in the checkout can swap it. That copy has to match the checksum the build wrote, and its signature has to verify against the key in `morphe-signing.pub`. One that changed after it was signed stops the release there instead of reaching Morphe Manager. The fixture runs, the release receipt and the index update read that same copy too, so they describe the bundle that's tagged and not whatever a later build left in the checkout.
- The whole-app walk follows the new settings layout. It opens each section on the main page and folds it again, and it checks the one-list view from the toggle under search before putting the toggle back the way it was.
- Changelog entries don't open with a "Threads:" label anymore. HushThreads only patches Threads, so it repeated itself on every line. The release scripts stopped adding or asking for it, and they drop it from any bullet that still has one when a release is cut.
- The bundle signing key comes from `HUSHTHREADS_BUNDLE_SIGNING_KEY` first and `MORPHE_SIGNING_KEY` second, so a shell that kept another repo's key doesn't fail the key check.
- A fresh checkout builds again. Dependency verification was missing the hash for junit-bom 5.13.1's module file, so Gradle stopped before compiling anything unless that file was already trusted locally.
- A release walk ties the installed APK to the bundle and the inputs it was patched from. Publish checks its manifest and identity again, and wants every screen covered with a clean result. A walk on an install that was already on the phone needs that install's patch receipt, and a stale or incomplete one is refused.
- The release description fixtures test conflicting build claims in the current facts now, ahead of the historical notes.
- The notice mirror check waits 400 ms between requests, so it doesn't draw rate limits when other Hush repos check the same mirrors at the same time.
- Fixture tests keep what they work out per build in soft references, with a 3 GB heap, so every variant fits in one run.
- The whole-app walk waits for each screen and scrolls to the row it wants, so a slow phone no longer reads as a failed walk. It also patches the same default selection Morphe Manager does. It used to apply every patch, `Change version code` included, and that left the phone on a build number no ordinary build could install over.
- The signed-app contracts find their sites by strings and shape instead of naming one build's classes, since a release checks every variant. They'd fallen behind on the move off 452 and again on 454, and caught up both times. On 454 they follow the feed merge's extra parameter, analytics sites that Threads now jumps onto, share tiles spread over several lambdas, and videos that reach the player through a helper holding autoplay off.
- A release build patches every variant of the Threads version it declares and stops if it finds none. Before this it picked one of two variants of the same version without saying so.
- Patching is checked with fingerprint validation on, in the fixture tests and in verify-all-patches.ps1, so a fingerprint that fits two methods of a build fails its patch. Before, the patcher hooked whichever of the two it found first.
- The source census can finish on GitLab again. It reads the watched paths of ReVanced's mirror through GitLab's GraphQL, a few questions for every branch at once, where it used to spend one of the roughly 60 hourly REST requests on each branch and path. Branches that share a head share one comparison. Forks GitLab has scheduled for deletion aren't counted, since a scanner keeps making and deleting them. A rate limit that resets more than five minutes out fails that source right away and says when to run again, so a run no longer sleeps for most of an hour.
- The source census report keeps two hits in a recorded repository apart when their paths differ only by case. It used to list one of them.
- The source census flags a recorded fork or copy when code search finds Threads files in it that its own lineage doesn't hold, even if another recorded source has them. Forks used to count as plain copies of their parent, so new Threads work in one passed a clean census unless an index listed it. GitHub's code search leaves most forks out, though, so this only reaches the ones it indexes. NexAlloy-XES, now gnadgnaoh/SexAlloy, is one it can't see. It has its own reviewed entry in the ledger now, with its files' blob ids pinned.
- A phone install doesn't stop halfway anymore when another session reads the phone's lease file at the same moment. It tries the file again for up to about four seconds before giving up.
- The source census asks GitLab for each branch's head together with its watched paths. A branch deleted partway through a run gets its own note now. It used to read as a branch that had moved to no Threads code. GitLab code search hits in a recorded fork or copy get their blob ids too, so new Threads files in a GitLab fork flag it the way GitHub hits already did. Several forks share one request for those ids, kept under GitLab's limit on how long a question can be, and two paths or branches that differ only in case each get their own blob id.

## Threads

- Don't want HushThreads settings in the menu you get by holding Threads' icon? Turn off the new `Settings shortcut on the app icon` switch on the Pause, backup and diagnostics page and it leaves that menu right away, while Threads' own shortcuts stay. A long press on the Threads logo and the HushThreads row in Threads' settings still open the settings, and Pause leaves the switch as you set it.
- Pressing and holding the text of an opened post brings up Copy text again, the same as in your feed, so you get the whole post with its links. It had stopped doing anything on 451. A new `Copy text on long press` switch under Posts in HushThreads settings turns this on or off. It starts on and comes with every build.
- Open links in browser now also covers the places on 451 that used to skip it. An ad's link button and a swipe up on an ad in the media viewer send the ad's web link to your browser the same way post links go, and so do the privacy policy and disclaimer links on a lead form. Meta's own pages still open in Threads.
- Search's Follow suggestions row is gone too. It has its own switch, `Hide follow suggestions in Search`, right under Hide suggested users on the Feed page, and it starts on. Nothing takes the row's place, and search results and topics stay as they are. Turn the switch off, or pause HushThreads, and Search looks the way Threads draws it.
- Save photo and Save all work on phones with smaller screens again. On a 720 px wide screen Threads only keeps a photo at up to 750 px, and HushThreads took every one of those for a thumbnail and saved nothing. It now saves the largest copy there is, still prefers a full size one when Threads has it, and still never saves an avatar-sized copy.
- Disable video autoplay now also tells Threads' video prefetcher to hold off. The switch only held a feed video at its cover frame, so Threads could still start downloading a held video ahead of time. The patch now answers the prefetcher's autoplay-off question itself, only where the prefetcher asks it, so Instagram's older autoplay checker is left alone. With the switch off, paused or in safe mode, Threads' own answer goes back as before. Checked on a Galaxy S22 with Threads 451. The prefetcher got the hold answer with the switch on and Threads' own with it off, and a tapped video still played full screen.
- The HushThreads settings home page has two new rows. `Quick setups` changes a set of switches in one tap: Quiet hides ads and suggested accounts, Privacy stops most usage reports, takes tracking off shared links and hides your screenshots from Threads, and Back to defaults puts every feature switch back. A toast says how many changed. `Report a problem` opens a new GitHub bug report with your HushThreads and Threads versions, your phone and the switches you have on already filled in.
- More settings is now a heading on the HushThreads settings home page, with Appearance, Links, Updates, Set when you patched, Pause, backup and diagnostics and About listed under it. Every page is one tap from home and Back always goes home. Report a problem and Support HushThreads are still the last two rows, and the patch descriptions and bug report form point to the shorter paths.
- Don't use Quick setups? Press and hold its row on the settings home page and it's gone, and its help line says so. To bring it back, tap the Quick setups row on the Pause, backup and diagnostics page. Screen readers get the same press and hold on that row, and no other row offers one.
- HushThreads settings stay open when Threads redraws itself, after you change the font size or switch dark theme from the quick settings, or when Android closes Threads in the background and you come back. They used to close. They now come back on the page you were on. That holds with the settings open over two Threads screens and one of them closed, and on Android 9 in split screen when the Threads side sits for more than 30 seconds before you tap back into it.
- A settings file you pick for Import or Export isn't lost anymore when Threads redraws itself while the file picker is open, after a font size or dark theme change, or when Android closes Threads in the background to make room. The settings came back as if you hadn't picked anything. The file picker now opens through a small invisible screen of HushThreads' own, which keeps your pick until the settings are back. Access to the file ends once it's read or written. If Android closes Threads before that, it ends the next time Threads starts. Two quick taps on Import or Export open one picker, not two.
- After an export or import, the Export settings or Import settings row says how it went, in full, until you run another. That message used to show only in a pop-up, and newer Android versions cut those off after two lines, so a refusal like a damaged file lost its "Nothing was changed."
- Save's messages are short enough to read whole on Android 12 and later, which cut a message after two lines. On an S22 the proxy message stopped mid-word, and the slow-download one was just as long. A carousel's result now shows each line as its own message, so a line under the counts, like a proxy asking for a password, isn't lost. The German, Spanish, Indonesian, Portuguese and Turkish wording was shortened to fit too.
- A download that only trickles in now stops after ten minutes per file and says it was too slow, instead of holding one of the three save slots for as long as the server likes. A host lookup that never answers gives up after 20 seconds, and Cancel now ends a save that's still waiting on one.
- Cancel and the download time limit now end a save even when the phone's proxy service stops answering. Waiting proxy calls share the fixed limit on background network checks, so repeated attempts can't keep creating threads.
- A save's download now has a connection of its own that never asks Threads' cookie store or sign-in prompts for anything, so it can't send a cookie or a password, and it drops every cookie a server or a redirect sets. It still goes through the proxy your Wi-Fi or phone settings name and checks the server's certificate the same way. If that proxy asks for a password, the save stops and tells you, since it never sends one.
- On Android 9, a save without Threads' Storage permission now stops before it downloads anything and tells you where to turn the permission on. A carousel stops fetching its remaining pages if the permission is taken away partway through.
- Joining the picture and sound of a VP9 save (or AV1 before Android 14) now stops before it would take more than 24 MB of memory, and the save falls back to the single file. A file built from millions of tiny parts can't run Threads out of memory that way anymore. Cancel is also noticed while the join is still reading the tracks.
- When a save finds no picture or video it can keep, the diagnostics report now lists the kind and size of every address it looked at, so a bug report shows why. It never includes the addresses themselves.
- When the regular Instagram app from Meta sits beside your patched Threads, the Links page in HushThreads settings says Instagram won't open Threads posts or profiles here. That's Instagram's own check, and it's why Instagram says it couldn't load the website.
- When the settings list can't be put on the HushThreads screen at all, the screen shows Retry and Back instead of staying blank. Retry opens the page you were headed to, with your switches as you left them.
- When Threads rebuilds its screen with the settings open (after a text size change, say, or when Android closed Threads in the background), a settings page that fails to come back now gives way to a fresh page. Before, that failure would have crashed Threads, since it happens where the settings' own Retry and Back can't catch it.
- TalkBack now reads the Threads logo at the top of the feed as "Threads". Before, it stopped on the refresh spinner inside the logo and said "Progress bar". The README also says the logo ignores taps and holds while the feed loads or refreshes.
- TalkBack no longer stops on the HushThreads settings list as a whole to offer a long press that does nothing there. Quick setups, the one row with a long press, still offers it.
- HushThreads now keeps a note of how each switch starts in the build you patched. When a later build changes how a switch starts, one you never changed keeps the setting it had. Earlier builds left no such note, so this starts working with the update after this one.
- Settings file access stays tracked when a disk write or Android's permission service fails. Cleanup retries after a restart, and retrying the same file can't keep lasting access without a saved cleanup record.
- Morphe Manager lists every change of the release your Threads was patched with, not just a short summary. For that one release Manager shows the patch bundle's description instead of the changelog, and the description was a paragraph while every older release listed its changes. It now goes on with the release's Threads bullets after the summary. You'll see it from the next release on.

## Tooling

- A GitHub description that names no release, patch count or Threads build now passes the release facts check and stays as written when a release publishes. Both used to refuse it, though a description like that has nothing a release can leave out of date. One that names any of those is still held to this release's and rewritten as before.
- The release cut now moves the release check test's User-Agent from whatever version it names. The v0.0.14 prep left that test on 0.0.13, so the next cut found nothing to move and stopped.
- The file picker behind Export settings and Import settings now has its own entry in the source ledger. Its two classes never had one, so the provenance test failed on every full run since they were added.
- When the final APK check catches the direct browser hook overwriting something Threads still needs, it now says which case it found. The register can be past the method's own locals, or Threads reads it right where the hook goes in, or Threads reads it once the link has opened. Each test build has to fail for its own reason, so one that trips the wrong part of the check doesn't pass anymore.
- Save's contract tests now cover the two other ways into Copy link's row call that would skip the Save row, a switch case and an exception handler aimed straight at it. The patch and the final APK check already refused both, but only a plain jump had a test, so losing either refusal would have gone unnoticed.
- The final APK check now holds Disable video autoplay's prefetch hold to its contract. Where Threads' prefetcher asks Instagram's autoplay-off question, the answer has to go through the extension right after it's read and come back in the same register, and every jump to the test that reads it has to pass through that call too. Nothing else may make the call. The question itself, its Olympus twin, Instagram's older autoplay checker and the prefetch dispatcher have to stay as Threads wrote them, and a build without the patch leaves every one of them alone. Each rule has a test build that only it refuses.
- The final APK check's browser guard has a test build only its completion half can catch: a link hook on a register that's free where the hook goes in but read again once the link has opened. No test build failed that half alone before, so losing it would have gone unnoticed.
- Save's final APK contract got stricter. A branch inside the post menu's Copy link case that jumps straight to the row call would skip the Save row, so the patch and the check both refuse one now. Share's jump onto Copy link's row still works. Every static method on the media bridge class has to be a bridge the patch writes, and written, so one left empty or one the patch doesn't know fails. A build without Save has every bridge and the activity reader checked as shipped, and a changed menu is reported at the first instruction that differs.
- The final APK check now holds Save photos and videos to its own contract. The post menu's Copy link path has to carry exactly one Save row, drawn with the calls Copy link's own row is built from and handed the menu and its composer, while every other menu item still reaches Copy link as before. The row's readers, its click and all fifteen media bridges have to point where the patch found them. A build without Save has to leave the menu and every stub as they shipped, and a bundle from before Save had a status reads as leaving it out.
- The build classpath inventory refuses to write when a project's buildscript graph is missing, instead of quietly leaving it out. That happens when a build doesn't evaluate every project, as under configure-on-demand, and the refusal names each one. Its Guava probe also stopped failing every Gradle command when it can't find one of the two plugins. It records no jar for that plugin now, and only the inventory refuses. A refused run also deletes the previous inventory, so nothing reads an old one as this run's.
- The same classpath now resolves commons-lang3 3.18.0 instead of the 3.16.0 the Morphe plugin asks for, which is inside GHSA-j288-q9x7-2f5v (CVE-2025-48924, 3.0 to 3.17.0). That was the last advisory OSV reported for the build's 114 plugin components, and the build advisory gate now finds none. It's a floor too, so it goes quiet once the plugin asks for 3.18.0 or later.
- The classpath the build plugins run from now resolves Guava 33.7.2-jre instead of 33.5.0-jre, which is inside GHSA-xxph-c9ww-hj94 (CVE-2026-102554, 4.0 to 33.7.1). It's a floor, so a plugin that later asks for a newer Guava still gets it. The build classpath inventory also records which jar the Morphe and Android Gradle plugins really load the advisory's three classes from, and it refuses to write when that isn't the Guava the classpath resolved. The bundle build and the focused registry tests pass with it.
- The source census now waits out a rate limit for as long as the answer says. GitLab throttles unauthenticated reads and answers 429 with the time its limit resets, and the census used to wait a flat 61 seconds, so a long reset used up its three tries and failed the run. It waits until the reset that Retry-After (seconds or a date), RateLimit-Reset or X-RateLimit-Reset names, plus a second, capped at 15 minutes by `-MaxRateLimitWaitSeconds`. An answer that names no reset still waits `-RateLimitWaitSeconds`, and a fourth limit in a row still fails the source. The run log also says whether GitLab was read with a token, since a token raises the limit.
- The source census reads the Morphe Patch Tracker again. Its list now carries a couple of bundles twice under keys that differ only in case (immortalzeus:dev and ImmortalZeus:dev), and the census refused the whole file as unreadable JSON. It reads those keys as they are now and counts each repository once, in PowerShell 7 and Windows PowerShell 5.1 alike.
- The final APK check now holds Hide suggested users on profiles to its own contract. It finds both places from the clean DEX alone: the profile screen's suggested accounts carousel, which has to hand its list to the extension right before Threads' own null check and cast the answer back, and the header row, which has to ask first thing on its path and leave by its check's other side through a local nothing reads. A build without the patch has to leave both as Threads wrote them, with no call to the extension anywhere.
- The final APK check now holds Copy text on long press to its own contract whenever Settings is selected. Every override check in the post row has to carry the patch's hook, which hands the override and its own action to the extension in a free local and casts the answer back, and PostText has to ask about its selection switch first thing. A build without Settings has to leave both exactly as Threads wrote them.
- The build classpath inventory now records a SHA-256 of settings.gradle.kts, patches/build.gradle.kts, gradle/libs.versions.toml and gradle/verification-metadata.xml, and the release receipt refuses an inventory whose hash for any of them differs from the checkout, naming the file. Before, only the settings script was checked, so a changed plugin version or dependency pin could leave an old inventory standing for the new build. Each hash is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the file's raw bytes.
- The source census reads Jman's Patch Bundle Registry now, through its registration file and the paged Threads list, because the old bundle files there answer 404. It follows the list's own total across short pages within a request and row budget, reads renamed repositories under their current names, and counts a repository as a Threads bundle only for a current release with verified metadata. History, unverified entries and a bare registration are reported but not promoted, and a list it can't finish reading fails the census. The source ledger points its Jman entry at the registry too, with HushThreads' registration there as the listing's evidence.
- Updated the build wrapper to Gradle 9.8.1, which fixes three high security advisories. The build advisory check now checks the recorded Gradle distribution separately from component libraries and refuses missing or unreadable version evidence, including when online component checks are skipped.
- A fixture test checks on 451 that both of the post row's long press override checks and PostText's selection flag go through the extension, and that a jump straight to an override check or a selection flag written over before PostText copies it stops the patch.
- The release receipt now asks OSV about the plugin classpath that builds and signs the bundle too, from an inventory settings.gradle.kts writes after each bundle build, and reports it apart from what the bundle carries, with its own exception list. A version that was only asked for and resolved to another is listed as a request, and a missing inventory or a dependency that didn't resolve stops the release instead of reading as clean.
- The bundle build holds the Android Gradle plugin's jose4j at 0.9.6 and jdom2 at 2.0.6.1, the patch releases that fix their high advisories, so the plugin classpath has none left.
